passage:
Jaya waited in the school corridor outside the counsellor's room until the bell had stopped ringing. Inside, Gautam, the counsellor, let her sit without speaking for a minute.
Then she said, "I sent money from Ma's account to someone who promised me a phone. It's gone." Her voice cracked. "Ma will be so angry. Papa too. I can't say it."
Gautam nodded slowly. "That sounds heavy. Most parents would rather hear the truth than find out later, and the sooner they know, the more can be done, like calling the bank. I can sit with you when you tell them."
Jaya looked at the floor, then nodded. That evening Gautam phoned her mother, and Jaya, sitting beside him, took the phone for the last part.

qa.q: What had Jaya been promised in return for the money?
qa.a: She had been promised a phone.

qa.q: Why did Jaya find it hard to say what happened?
qa.a: She fears that Ma will be angry, and Papa too, and she feels ashamed, so her voice cracked.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do to help Jaya tell her parents?
qa.a: Gautam let her sit quietly, explained that most parents prefer the truth and that quick action can limit the damage, and offered to sit with her when she tells them. 🤍

qa.q: How might Jaya's mother feel when she hears?
qa.a: She may feel shock and worry about the money, but probably more concern for her daughter, who came forward instead of hiding it.

grounding: Shows a teen afraid to tell her parents about a scam, encouraged by a counsellor to tell early.

passage:
Friday night

I've been sick in my stomach for two days. On Wednesday I saw an offer for cheap game coins: "90% off, today only." I used Mummy's phone payment app while she was bathing, because I knew her PIN. 1,500 rupees. No coins came. The site vanished.

I kept thinking, she'll kill me. She'll never trust me again. So I said nothing. Every time her phone buzzed, my heart jumped.

Today Himani didi found me crying behind the water tank. When I told her, she said, "The longer you wait, the harder it is for the bank to do anything. Tell her now."

So I did, at dinner. My voice shook. I said, "Mummy, I got scammed and I used your money. I'm really sorry."

She went quiet. Then she said, "I'm upset you used my phone. But I'm glad you told me." She called the bank helpline straight away and reported it to the cybercrime number too. We'll change her PIN tomorrow.

I feel lighter than I have in two days.

Divyansh

qa.q: How much money did Divyansh lose on the fake game coins?
What was Divyansh feeling in the two days before telling Mummy?
qa.a: Divyansh felt sick with fear and shame, scared she would never trust Divyansh again.

qa.q: Why was Himani didi's advice important?
qa.a: She pointed out that waiting makes it harder for the bank to act, so telling early could limit the damage.

qa.q: How did Mummy react, and why did it help?
qa.a: Mummy was upset but glad to be told, and called the bank and cybercrime number straight away, which showed that the truth was better than hiding it.

grounding: It shows a teen afraid to tell a parent after being scammed, learning that telling early lets the parent act quickly and limit the damage.

passage:
Yash: i did something dumb
Santosh: what
Yash: sold my old phone on a buy-sell site. buyer said he'd pay by UPI. sent me a link to "receive" money
Yash: i clicked and entered my pin. 4000 went OUT of papa's account instead
Santosh: oh no
Yash: that was yesterday. i haven't told papa. i can't. he saved for that account
Santosh: yash u have to tell him today
Yash: he'll be so angry
Santosh: maybe. but if the bank knows fast they can sometimes stop it. every hour matters
Yash: i feel so stupid
Santosh: they trick adults too. my uncle lost more last year
Santosh: tell him now. i'll wait here

Yash walked into the living room and told his father everything. Papa closed his eyes for a second, then said, "Thank you for telling me today." He called the bank to block the account and dialled the cybercrime helpline while Yash sat beside him.

qa.q: How much money went out of Papa's account?
What was Yash feeling about telling Papa?
qa.a: Yash felt ashamed and afraid, sure that Papa would be very angry.

qa.q: Why did Santosh push Yash to tell Papa the same day?
qa.a: Santosh knew that if the bank is told fast it can sometimes stop the loss, so every hour mattered.

qa.q: How did Papa respond when Yash told him?
qa.a: Papa thanked Yash for telling him that day and immediately called the bank and the cybercrime helpline.

grounding: It shows a teen afraid to tell a parent after a scam, encouraged by a friend to tell early, and a parent acting quickly to limit the damage.
